assessments.reasoning: Section 6.5 begins on printed p. 21 and gives the assignment and restoration rule on p. 22. It makes assignments to local iterator variables and restores earlier identifier values when the iterator exits. The grammar separates a bound identifier from the discard placeholder and from an expression or identifier that supplies the collection.

challenge.method: Read the scoping paragraph and all three simple-iterator productions. Checked an already-bound identifier, an identifier merely supplying the collection, the discard placeholder, and Dewar's different iterator finalization rule on printed p. 85.
challenge.results: Restoration applies to an identifier actually bound as a local by the simple iterator. The discard placeholder binds no identifier. Dewar's 1979 SETL rule about setting iteration variables to om on normal loop completion belongs to a different titled reference and cannot extend or displace Levin's rule.

limitations: The text documents iterator-local bindings in this ISETL manual and leaves interruption and failure behavior unsettled.
